one_sentence: The bilateral audit reveals that science borrows ten unprovable assumptions from theology, creating a structural contradiction that prevents genuine dialogue.
executive_summary: This document argues that the 80/20 split between science and religion in public discourse is based on a broken premise: science operates on ten assumptions (e.g., external world exists, logic works) that it cannot prove experimentally, yet it borrowed these from theology without acknowledgment. The bilateral audit holds both sides to the same standard—falsifiability, predictive power—and finds six leak points in naturalism (consciousness, mathematical effectiveness, moral obligation, information origin, fine-tuning, initial conditions) while theology holds on biblical predictions and moral dynamics. The method yields a coherence/decoherence framework: coherence is narrow, decoherence is easy, restoration requires external input. This structural finding, surfaced across seventy domains, suggests Christianity provides the most complete account of the discovered architecture, challenging the current science-religion settlement.
short_summary: This document is a formal proposal for a bilateral audit of science and religion, holding both to the same epistemic standards. The core structural claim is that science's 80% public authority rests on ten borrowed, unprovable assumptions from theology, creating a contradiction that prevents genuine dialogue. Key evidence includes six leak points in naturalism (e.g., consciousness, fine-tuning) and theology's predictive accuracy on physical claims, plus a coherence/decoherence pattern across seventy domains. This matters because it reframes the science-religion boundary as a structural contradiction rather than a settled division, offering a new method for resolution.
